items.title: Bounded BV data on the real line
items.statement: The bounded, locally integrable translation-variation class BV_b(R), with no L1(R) tail requirement.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §2.3.1, pp. 19–20: one-dimensional BV seminorms and the spatial translation estimate used in the scheme analysis.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.6, Theorems 4.18–4.19, PDF pp. 55–57: the BV convention, Helly compactness and the L1-data convergence theorem.

items.title: Monotone finite-volume scheme and invariant-interval CFL
items.statement: A locally Lipschitz, consistent, coordinatewise monotone two-point flux and conservative cell-average update under the full invariant-interval CFL bound lambda(L1+L2)<=1.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §§2.2.2–2.2.3, pp. 15–18: monotone numerical fluxes, invariant-range CFL and standard Godunov/Lax–Friedrichs fluxes.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.4.4, PDF pp. 49–50: local Lipschitz monotone fluxes and the CFL condition; §4.6, pp. 55–57: convergence hypotheses.

items.title: Piecewise-linear time interpolant of a finite-volume scheme
items.statement: The affine-in-time, cellwise-constant reconstruction between consecutive monotone finite-volume states.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §2.3.1, pp. 19–21: discrete time-variation estimates for the finite-volume state.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: Theorem 4.19, §4.6, PDF p. 56: the precise affine-in-time interpolant on each cell and time slab.

items.title: Invariant range, TVD and time increments for a monotone finite-volume update
items.statement: The full CFL makes the update map isotone and constant-preserving, giving invariant range, discrete TVD and a summed time-increment bound.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: Proposition 2.3.1 and its proof, §2.3.1, PDF pp. 19–20 (space TVD); Proposition 2.3.3, p. 20 (time increments).

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: Lemma 4.13 and Lemma 4.14, §§4.5.3–4.5.4, PDF pp. 52–54: TVD and time-continuity estimates for monotone schemes.

items.title: Discrete Kruzhkov inequality for a monotone finite-volume scheme
items.statement: The Crandall–Majda numerical entropy flux G_k yields the exact one-step discrete Kruzhkov inequality for every real entropy level.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: Proposition 2.3.6 and its proof, §2.3.2, PDF pp. 21–22: the discrete entropy flux built from componentwise maxima/minima.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.2, Proposition 4.10, PDF pp. 50–51: the numerical entropy flux and its derivation from monotonicity.

items.title: Local compactness and initial trace for BV finite-volume states
items.statement: A rational-point diagonal plus temporal translation bound gives local strong compactness, the exact initial trace, and a common limit of affine and piecewise-constant reconstructions.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: Propositions 2.3.1 and 2.3.3, §2.3.1, PDF pp. 19–21: spatial BV and discrete time-increment estimates.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: Theorems 4.18–4.19, §4.6, PDF pp. 55–57: Helly compactness and the affine-in-time interpolant. The rational-point proof and nonintegrable-data trace argument are supplied locally.

items.title: Strong entropy convergence of monotone finite-volume schemes
items.statement: For scalar C1 flux and bounded BV data, a consistent monotone locally Lipschitz flux under the full invariant CFL and positive lower time-to-space ratio converges strongly locally to the unique Kruzhkov solution, with separate DC and non-DC data branches.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §§2.2–2.3.3, PDF pp. 13–23: monotone fluxes, invariant bounds, TVD/time increments, the discrete entropy inequality and convergence under a CFL condition. The local compactness and initial-trace proofs are supplied here.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.4.4–4.6, PDF pp. 49–57, especially Proposition 4.10, Lemmas 4.13–4.14, Theorem 4.18 and Theorem 4.19. The book proof covers L1 data and uses a global-tail argument; the nonintegrable BV branch is proved locally here.

items.title: A consistent nonmonotone flux selects a nonentropy expansion shock
items.statement: A smooth consistent shared-face flux with negative first derivative at (-1,0) preserves a strongly convergent stationary Burgers expansion shock that violates the k=0 Kruzhkov inequality.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §2.3.2–2.3.3, PDF pp. 21–23: discrete entropy inequalities and why they are needed in addition to weak conservation.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.2, PDF pp. 50–51: entropy admissibility is a separate inequality beyond the weak conservation law.

items.title: Burgers Godunov flux under the invariant-interval CFL bound
items.statement: On [-M,M], the Burgers Godunov flux is coordinatewise monotone and M-Lipschitz in each coordinate, so lambda<=1/(2M) satisfies the full CFL and the convergence theorem applies.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §2.2.3, pp. 17–18: Godunov flux and monotonicity under a CFL condition; §2.3.3, pp. 22–23: convergence.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.4.4, p. 50 (Godunov flux is monotone and locally Lipschitz); §4.6, pp. 55–57 (monotone-scheme convergence).

items.title: Lax–Friedrichs flux under the invariant-interval CFL bound
items.statement: With alpha>=sup_I|f'|, the Lax–Friedrichs flux has coordinate Lipschitz constants (L+alpha)/2 and is monotone; lambda(L+alpha)<=1 yields convergence under the theorem.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §2.2.3, pp. 17–18: the Lax–Friedrichs numerical flux and its monotonicity condition; §2.3.3, pp. 22–23: convergence.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.4.4, p. 49: partial derivatives of the Lax–Friedrichs flux and the CFL condition; §4.6, pp. 55–57: convergence.

items.title: Godunov scheme captures a stationary Burgers entropy shock
items.statement: The aligned 1-to--1 Burgers shock has common Godunov face flux 1/2, is stationary at every grid level, has Rankine–Hugoniot speed zero, and satisfies every Kruzhkov inequality.

references.title: Jérôme Droniou, A beginner’s course in finite volume approximation of scalar conservation laws, complete lecture note
references.locator: §§2.3.3–2.4, PDF pp. 22–24: monotone-scheme entropy convergence and numerical Burgers shock examples.

references.title: Siddhartha Mishra, Ulrik S. Fjordholm and Rémi Abgrall, Numerical Methods for Conservation Laws, ETH lecture notes
references.locator: §4.4, PDF pp. 40–44 (Godunov/Lax–Friedrichs fluxes and Burgers shocks); §4.6, pp. 55–57 (entropy convergence).
